walkthroughs.body_html:
Mensuration — a core area of GCSE Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Mensuration brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Mensuration.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

options: π

mcqs.q: What is the difference between area and perimeter?
options: Area and perimeter are different names for the same measurement.
The acceleration of the object.
Perimeter is the total distance around the outside; area is the amount of surface inside (measured in square units).
Area is half the perimeter for any shape.

mcqs.q: On a speed-time graph, what does the area under the line represent?
options: The total speed achieved.
The distance travelled.
The acceleration of the object.
5, because that is the middle value.

mcqs.q: What is the range of the data set [4, 7, 2, 9, 5]?
options: Area is half the perimeter for any shape.
5, because that is the middle value.
From 2 to 9 — the range is given as two values.
7 — the largest minus the smallest (9 - 2).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Rational number”?
options: Whole number greater than 1 with exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
A number that can be written as a fraction of two integers (e.g. 1/2, -3, 0.75).
Result of multiplying an integer by itself (1, 4, 9, 16, 25…).
A whole number, positive, negative or zero (e.g. -3, 0, 17).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Cube number”?
options: A whole number, positive, negative or zero (e.g. -3, 0, 17).
Result of multiplying an integer by itself three times (1, 8, 27, 64…).
A number that can be written as a fraction of two integers (e.g. 1/2, -3, 0.75).
Whole number greater than 1 with exactly two factors: 1 and itself.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Square number”?
options: A whole number, positive, negative or zero (e.g. -3, 0, 17).
Result of multiplying an integer by itself (1, 4, 9, 16, 25…).
A number that cannot be written as a fraction; its decimal goes on without repeating (e.g. √2, π).
A number that can be written as a fraction of two integers (e.g. 1/2, -3, 0.75).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Prime number”?
options: A number that cannot be written as a fraction; its decimal goes on without repeating (e.g. √2, π).
Whole number greater than 1 with exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
Result of multiplying an integer by itself (1, 4, 9, 16, 25…).
A number that can be written as a fraction of two integers (e.g. 1/2, -3, 0.75).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Integer”?
options: Whole number greater than 1 with exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
Result of multiplying an integer by itself three times (1, 8, 27, 64…).
A whole number, positive, negative or zero (e.g. -3, 0, 17).
Result of multiplying an integer by itself (1, 4, 9, 16, 25…).

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Irrational number”?
options: A whole number, positive, negative or zero (e.g. -3, 0, 17).
A number that cannot be written as a fraction; its decimal goes on without repeating (e.g. √2, π).
Whole number greater than 1 with exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
Result of multiplying an integer by itself three times (1, 8, 27, 64…).
